ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $DE\parallel BC$, $S_{\triangle ADE} = S_{\text{trapezoid } DBCE}$, then what is the ratio $DE: BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that, $S_{\triangle ADE}=S_{\text{trapezoid} DBCE}$,\\
then $S_{\triangle ADE} : S_{\triangle ABC} = 1 : 2$,\\
since $DE \parallel BC$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$,\\
let the similarity ratio be $k$,\\
then the ratio of the areas is $k^2 = \frac{1}{2}$,\\
thus the similarity ratio is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
therefore $DE : BC = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a triangle ABC, with A at the upper vertex, and B and C below forming the base BC. Point D is on side AB, point E is on side AC, and segment DE connects D and E, and from the figure DE appears parallel to the base BC. DE divides the large triangle into the small triangle ADE above and the trapezoid DBCE below. Reasoning: It is known that S_{triangle ADE}=S_{trapezoid DBCE}. The whole triangle ABC is composed of triangle ADE and trapezoid DBCE, so S_{triangle ABC}=S_{triangle ADE}+S_{trapezoid DBCE}=2S_{triangle ADE}; therefore S_{triangle ADE}:S_{triangle ABC}=1:2. Because DE∥BC, triangle ADE and triangle ABC are similar. Let the similarity ratio k=DE/BC; then the area ratio is equal to the square of the similarity ratio, that is, k^2=1/2. Thus k=sqrt(1/2)=sqrt(2)/2. Therefore DE:BC=sqrt(2):2.
